about: Gates of `gstore-bench check` / `compare` / `ci` (see bench/README.md). Exact gates always apply. Timing gates are one-sided and calibration-normalized: a measured time m is divided by clamp(calib_measured / calib_baseline) and compared with the baseline time b as (m + floor_ms) / (b + floor_ms). Per query the floor is 0.1 ms, so a sub-millisecond query slowed 50x fails (review infra#2). The per-backend query geomean takes every query's (m + 0.05 ms) / (b + 0.05 ms), each clamped to [1/3, 3]; its limit is max(max_ratio, the baseline run's own process-to-process spread) but at most max_spread (review infra#4). Memory: (m + floor_mib) / (b + floor_mib). Sizes: m / b. A failing timing or memory gate re-runs only the failing phases, up to `retries` times, keeping the minimum of the medians. `bless` (and `ci`, of its baseline) refuses a debug build, a dirty tree, the library builder, a load above max_load_per_cpu per CPU and a run whose spread exceeds geomean.max_spread (review infra#10).
